verify:e-read: core.md §14.4 versus CORE-SNAP-003: an archive row with is_event true and a recurrence imports as kind routine (§15.3 step 10). §14.4 ghosts every row whose kind is not event, so its blocks become ghosts. Reproduced in the probe: 1 ghost on the block's day. Today's per-day scan (phone.rs:2409-2421, planner.rs:174-187) passes is_event=true and recurrence None, so it takes the event branch, has no deadline, and places nothing. The code follows §14.4's text, but that text also says the result 'equals today's per-day scan', and CORE-SNAP-003 requires exactly today's ghosts; for this legacy shape the two cannot both hold. Readings: (a) kind-based, as now; (b) skip rows whose legacy is_event was true, which the board no longer records. No fixture has such a row.

impl:d2-rulings: Spec change 5, §16 catalogue: compile now uses `core/cap_board` (400, 'The board is full.'), `core/bad_id` (400, 'The id counter belongs to another device.') and `core/notes_stale` (400, 'The notes changed on another device.'). The earlier draft message 'Those notes have changed since you started editing.' is gone from the crate. §16 should list these three rows, plus the restore `core/id_taken` and G8 `core/rules` compile rows.

impl:d2-rulings: Spec change 5, §13.3 G3, a case the ruling does not cover: a naive time inside the instant range whose local day falls in 1969 or 10000 (e.g. 1969-12-31T23:30 at UTC−1, which resolves to 1970-01-01T00:30Z) is not 'outside the range', so it still gets G3's year clause: `core/intent_json` 'not a time'. I kept that, since it is the spec's text, and pinned it in a compile.json vector. If you wanted every out-of-range naive time to be `core/date_range`, the G3 year clause needs rewording, and that one vector flips.

impl:d2-rulings: Spec change 5, §5.4 and the ruling's formula: the check applies only to `local_at(d, clamp(m, 0, 1439))`. If m is in the range but the 60-minute step lands outside it, `from_local` gives none and compile answers `core/bad_time`. This happens only on the last hour of 9999-12-31 inside a real gap, which no real zone has. Worth one sentence in the spec text.

impl:d2-rulings: Spec change 5, §13.3 G6/G7 ordering as built: bad_id, then the row's steps, then the G8 rules check, then the size check (`core/cap_board`), then any mint failure (`core/cap_items` or `core/cap_blocks` from a spent minter). Before this step, a spent minter answered inside the row, ahead of G8. The spec could say outright that a minter with no number left is reported after G6 and G8.

impl:d2-rulings: §20 / docs: `LogCommand::to_canonical` now panics on an integer above 2^53−1. Its doc comment says so, mirroring `BoardData::to_canonical_bytes`. If §20 describes it as infallible, it needs the same panic note.

impl:c3-ics-bounds: Ported test conflict, settled by the brief's bound 5: today's a_tzid_the_file_never_defined_falls_back_to_local_and_says_which_one_it_was (ics/tests.rs) asserted that the problem line quotes the TZID ('W. Europe Standard Time'). Bound 5 and CORE-GEN-010 forbid that, while settled point 1 says ported tests keep their expected values. I kept the expected start (540), renamed the test to ..._and_says_so_without_quoting_it, and it now asserts one generic line. The c2 test an_undefined_tzid_is_read_as_wall_time_in_every_zone changed the same way. The undefined-zone text now reads 'a time zone the file never defined, or defined past what can be read; read as this computer's'. The CALSCALE error now reads 'that calendar is written in a calendar other than the Gregorian, which this cannot read'. Spec change 5 should say whether the line may name which zone was guessed at; I took: it may not.

impl:c3-ics-bounds: Not covered by the brief, measured (Limits::default()): every event and every observance with a rule may walk the full max_rule_steps (100,000). 20,000 events of `DTSTART:00010101T090000` with `RRULE:FREQ=DAILY` (about 1.4 MB, no occurrences) cost about 1.6 ms each in release (10 ms in debug), so about 31 s release and over 3 minutes debug. That breaks DEV-ICS-004's 20 s. The 512-observance case is similar: 512 DAILY observances from year 1 (57 KB) take 0.9 s release and 4.7 s debug. This is the product max_events × max_rule_steps, which is bounded by the limits but large. A shared step budget per file (or per zone), or a skip-ahead for DAILY and WEEKLY rules without COUNT or BYSETPOS, would fix it. Either changes behaviour on hostile files only, but it is a new bound, so it is yours to rule on; I did not add it.

impl:c3-ics-bounds: Order dependence that is left: when a file goes over max_occurrences, parse keeps the first events' occurrences (take(room) before the sort). Overlay::sealed truncates to EVENTS_MAX (5,000) before it sorts. So a calendar past those limits still depends on listing order. Two overrides with the same RECURRENCE-ID resolve by file order, as today. Bound 6 covers ties only, so I left these alone.

impl:c3-ics-bounds: The per-event cap is not exact: as today, the check runs after each start's span is cut, so one event can reach max_occurrences_per_event + 399 occurrences (spread's 400-day guard). Overrides now count towards the cap and are expanded only into the room left. I took 'the per-event cap holds' to mean this bound, not a strict truncation, because truncating would change today's output for long multi-day series near 1,000 starts.

impl:c3-ics-bounds: Timing harness: the timed tests use ProptestConfig { timeout: 30_000, cases: 1 } with Just(()) (one case each). They are not properties, so common.md's 'default case count' rule is not applied to them; the real property tests in the file use the default count. Proptest writes tests/*.proptest-regressions on any failure; a stale one makes a timed case run once per saved seed. You may want it ignored in git (that is outside the crate).
